result: the mouse inventory, counted from positions, the ATAC peak calls and the boundaries alone -- before any RNA value is read
question: The domain rule attributes a non-coding element to a gene. Between genes, where no rule can name the gene whose body the element sits in, does the gene with the nearest 5' end inside the element's boundary-delimited domain match the element's own tissue more often than the gene with the nearest 5' end on the chromosome? Two invertebrates DISAGREE about exactly this stratum -- the worm's domain rule is ahead by +3.73 points [+2.79, +4.74] on 2,335 between-gene elements and still ahead at +4.47 [+3.16, +5.78] after its own outron exclusion, while the fly's is +0.12 [-0.25, +0.61] on 3,265 brain elements, no difference detected -- and NOBODY HAS ASKED A MAMMAL. This is that question in the mouse.

source_chosen.rna: ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq, Mus musculus embryo (14.5 days), the SAME 12 tissues, Barbara Wold lab (Caltech), ENCODE3; the file read per tissue is the experiment's own preferred-default `gene quantifications` TSV on mm10 with GENCODE M21, and the column read is TPM
source_chosen.boundaries: Bonev et al. 2017 (Cell 171:557-572.e24, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2017.09.043, GEO GSE96107), Table S2 'Genomic Coordinates and Compartment Identity of the Topological Domains in Different Cell Types': the authors' own insulation-score domain call on mm10, read as the domain edges. The primary sheet is `ncx NPC` -- neural progenitors FACS-purified from EMBRYONIC NEOCORTEX, in vivo -- 2,398 domains. The other four sheets and three ENCODE e14.5 CTCF sets are beside
source_chosen.boundary_caveat: Bonev's domains are read as their edges -- every domain start and end, deduplicated -- which is the only conversion and has no parameter. The three ENCODE e14.5 CTCF sets reported beside take every conservative-IDR peak as a boundary, which is the brief's CTCF option and not a Hi-C domain call. 4D Nucleome's 110 mm10 boundary BEDs are NOT used: they are DCIC-pipeline calls rather than author calls, the portal requires a login, and the portal states no licence
source_chosen.encode_licence: ENCODE data-use policy as encodeproject.org states it: released ENCODE data carry no restriction on use or publication; recorded from the portal, not inferred
source_chosen.one_source_for_both_modalities: ENCODE, one stage (embryonic day 14.5) and the SAME TWELVE TISSUE NAMES on both sides. The vocabulary is the source's own: the twelve are exactly the biosample term names that have both an ATAC-seq and a polyA plus RNA-seq experiment at e14.5, and no tissue is grouped, renamed or split here. ENCODE's e14.5 `brain` experiment is excluded because it contains forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain, which are three of the twelve. The accessibility and the RNA come from different animals of the same strain and stage, not the same nuclei, and that is stated in the reading.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
